articles.title: 4 Canadian soldiers killed, dozens injured after fast-moving fire erupts at military base
articles.summary: Four service members were killed and 39 hospitalized after high winds fueled a fast-moving fire at a Canadian military base in Alberta, officials said.
articles.body: Canadian officials said Sunday that four service members were killed and dozens more injured after a fast-moving fire swept through soldiers conducting live-fire training at a military base in Alberta. The deadly fire erupted Saturday at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, where a sudden shift in powerful winds sent flames sweeping toward troops training in the area, according to The Associated Press. Officials said 39 people were hospitalized, including 19 in critical condition. Eight others were listed as stable, while 12 were being treated for less serious injuries. Maj. Gen. Wade Rutland, commander of the Edmonton-based 1st Canadian Division, said military officials had been aware of the fire for hours but believed it was contained enough for training to continue, AP reported. AT LEAST 1 KILLED, 34 FIREFIGHTERS AND EMS WORKERS INJURED IN 'MAJOR' STATEN ISLAND SHIPYARD EXPLOSION: FDNY "The fire was a kilometer away when the wind shifted. That is not normal for a fire to move a kilometer in 36 seconds," Rutland said. Investigators have not yet determined what sparked the fire. Those killed were identified by the military as Sgt. Morgan Wong and Privates Shaun Farrell, Aidan Goulding and Hayden Lykkemark, AP reported. Wong was a member of the Loyal Edmonton Regiment, while the three others belonged to the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia’s Canadian Light Infantry. All four were serving with the Edmonton-based battalion. Prime Minister Mark Carney called the blaze one of the worst peacetime tragedies to strike Canada's armed forces on home soil, according to Reuters. WATCH: VIRGINIA COPS CRAWL THROUGH BURNING HOUSE TO SAVE MAN TRAPPED IN FIRE "I cannot recall such an incident in my short time for sure as a minister, but I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory," Canadian Defense Minister David McGuinty told reporters. The 39 injured people were being treated at hospitals in Wainwright, Edmonton, Red Deer and Calgary. Air ambulances from Edmonton and Saskatoon were also sent to the base Saturday to help transport patients. Several hospitals across Alberta activated a "Code Orange," an emergency designation used for mass-casualty incidents, as medical personnel prepared to treat the wounded. Military and civilian firefighters battled the flames through the night as intense winds fueled the fire. MARINE CORPS OSPREY CATCHES FIRE DURING EXERCISE IN NORTH CAROLINA; 4 INJURED The fire crossed the base perimeter into the surrounding area, but officials said no evacuation orders were issued. By Sunday, local authorities said the blaze was not expected to spread beyond its existing boundaries. He also praised emergency crews who battled the flames through the night. Fox News Digital's Michael Sinkewicz, Reuters and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Foreigner alleges rape by man she met online in Goa
articles.summary: Goa Police file FIR after foreign tourist alleges rape by man met on social media in Mandrem; case moved to Panaji women’s police station amid coordination issues.
articles.body: PANAJI: Goa police have registered an FIR against a man for allegedly raping a 45-year-old foreign tourist at the coastal village of Mandrem.Police said the survivor got in touch with the accused on social media and made plans to meet in Goa.The survivor, a divorcee, is European and had subsequently acquired another country’s nationality. She arrived in New Delhi in Aug before travelling to Goa and has been staying at Mandrem, police said.The survivor, in her complaint, said that she met the accused at the beach and later went to a room, where they consumed alcohol. Police said that as the woman was under the influence of alcohol, she could not resist when the accused person sexually assaulted her.Police said the incident was initially reported at Mandrem police station, but subsequently shifted to the women police station in Panaji, as there was no proper coordination between Mandrem police and the survivor.Goa police statistics reveal that on average, the state sees four women raped or sexually assaulted every week. From 2021 to 2025, a total of 922 women—aged between five and 70—were either raped or sexually assaulted.Police said that higher reporting and registration of offences in Goa reflect greater public awareness, easier access to police mechanisms, and increased public confidence in approaching law enforcement agencies.(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Goa | Silver Rate in Goa | Bank Holidays in Goa | Public Holidays in Goa | Petrol Price in GoaStay updated with the latest Goa news. articles.title: In 1968, Cassandra Henderson graduated from a North Carolina school; nearly 60 years later, she moved back into the same building after it was restored from 20 years of vacancy into 53 senior apartments
articles.summary: Cassandra Henderson graduated from Dillard Junior High in Yanceyville, North Carolina, in 1968.
articles.body: Cassandra Henderson graduated from Dillard Junior High in Yanceyville, North Carolina, in 1968. Nearly six decades later, she moved back into the same building, not as a student but as a resident of the newly restored Dillard School Senior Apartments. The former school, which had stood empty for about 20 years, has been transformed into 53 affordable apartments for seniors aged 62 and older, reported Tax Credit Coalition.The project is a rare example of a community turning a vacant historic building into practical housing. Originally built between 1949 and 1951, the Caswell County Training School was the first African American school in Caswell County to offer 11 grades. After desegregation in 1969, it was renamed for longtime principal Nicholas Longworth Dillard and continued serving students until it closed in 2002. Read more details about it here, as per Tax Credit Coalition's report:A school with deep local meaningFor generations of Black students in Caswell County, the school was more than a place to learn. It represented opportunity at a time when educational access was shaped by segregation. Its early name, Caswell County Training School, reflected the era’s segregated school system, but the institution became a centre of learning, pride and community life.The campus included a gymnasium addition in 1960, giving students space for athletics and gatherings beyond the classroom. Henderson’s graduation in 1968 came near the end of that era, just before desegregation changed the school’s role and identity. After desegregation, the school was renamed Dillard Junior High in honour of Nicholas Longworth Dillard, its longtime principal. The building continued to serve local students until its closure in 2002, after which it entered a long period of vacancy, as per the report.From empty building to senior housingFor two decades, the former school sat unused. Its future was uncertain until community-led preservation efforts helped secure its place on the National Register of Historic Places and build support for a new purpose.The restoration converted former classrooms into seven studio apartments and 46 one-bedroom apartments. All 53 units are restricted to seniors with incomes at or below 50 percent of the area median income, making the development an important affordable-housing option in rural Yanceyville. The project was developed through the work of DreamKey Partners and Red Stone Equity Partners. It also received recognition from the Affordable Housing Tax Credit Coalition, which awarded Dillard School Senior Apartments its 2026 Recognition of Housing Tax Credit Excellence in the Rural Housing category.Designed for ageing in placeThe apartments were designed to be more than simply affordable. The building includes elevator-served accessibility, a community centre with a business and computer room, fitness space, community laundry, tenant storage and on-site management with supportive service coordination, it was further reported.Outdoor amenities were also built into the plan. Residents have access to community gardens and recreation areas, including pickleball and shuffleboard courts, encouraging neighbours to stay active and connected.For Henderson, returning to the building meant rejoining a place filled with personal history. For other residents it provides a stable home in a familiar community with services and shared spaces designed for later life.Why adaptive reuse is importantThe Dillard School project is an example of how historic preservation and affordable housing can go hand in hand. Rather than demolish a prominent local feature, the community preserved its structure and repurposed it to fulfilll a present-day need.Many rural areas face particular housing problems such as little new building, an aging population and a limited choice of rented accommodation. Converting an existing school building into senior apartments can preserve local character while creating homes close to the people and places residents already know.The project also demonstrates the value of patient, community-led redevelopment. The school’s revival did not happen quickly. It required years of vacancy, preservation advocacy, historic recognition and investment before it could become housing again.A homecoming with a larger lessonCassandra Henderson’s return gives the Dillard School Senior Apartments a human story at their centre. A building that once shaped her education now provides her with a home, nearly 60 years after she walked its halls as a student.The transformation also offers a broader lesson for towns considering the future of vacant schools, factories and civic buildings. When communities protect historic places and adapt them carefully, they can retain memory while addressing urgent needs such as senior housing.Today, Dillard School Senior Apartments is a preserved landmark and active community. The 53 apartments are more than brick and classrooms returned; they are a new lease on life for a building that continues to serve the people of Yanceyville.You use AI every day. articles.title: Venezuela opposition renews support for Maria Corina Machado as leader
articles.summary: The exiled Nobel laureate has petitioned for new elections in Venezuela and for the country to allow her return.
articles.body:
An alliance of Venezuelan opposition parties has reaffirmed its commitment to exiled Nobel Peace Prize laureate Maria Corina Machado as its leader.

On Sunday, members of the opposition’s Unitary Democratic Platform (PUD) agreed in a meeting in Caracas to “recognise and support the leadership of Maria Corina Machado”.

The coalition also renewed its demand for free elections in Venezuela, following a series of contested presidential votes in 2024 and 2018.

Sunday’s statement included 14 proposals for a democratic transition, including freedom for political parties, the release of all political prisoners and the safe return of those who went into exile.

The announcement also increases pressure on authorities to allow Machado’s return. She has been living in exile since leaving Venezuela last December to receive her Nobel Prize.

“The will of the Venezuelans must once again govern the destiny of our nation,” the opposition’s former presidential candidate Edmundo Gonzalez wrote on social media supporting the proposals.

“We will not accept political prisoners, persecution or a governing power that disregards the mandate of its citizens. Living in freedom and under a genuine constitutional order is a legitimate demand of our society.”

Venezuela has yet to declare a date for a new presidential vote. Since January 3, the country has been led by interim President Delcy Rodriguez of the long-governing United Socialist Party of Venezuela (PSUV).

PSUV leaders have been accused of carrying out human rights abuses against political dissidents, including arbitrary arrest, imprisonment and torture.

Still, after the United States launched a military operation to abduct and jail former President Nicolas Maduro, the PSUV has remained in power with the support of the White House.

US President Donald Trump has backed Rodriguez’s leadership, despite her having been Maduro’s vice president.

His administration has maintained an active role in Venezuela, exerting control over its oil resources and pressuring the Rodriguez government for reforms.

But critics point out that Trump has been reluctant to push Rodriguez for new elections, opting instead for a three-phase plan that focuses first on stabilising the country and economic recovery before pursuing a political transition.

Machado, meanwhile, has told The Financial Times she would like to see Venezuela hold elections by July next year.

“The US government and the Venezuelan people all agree ⁠⁠that the only way to make ⁠⁠this sustainable and ⁠⁠a real victory is to turn Venezuela into a stable democracy,” she told the newspaper earlier this month.

Venezuelan authorities blocked Machado’s repeated attempts to return to the country, according to her party, Vente Venezuela.

Machado has also reportedly attempted to petition the Trump administration for help re-entering Venezuela.

Separately, she gifted Trump her Nobel Peace Prize in January, during a visit to Washington, DC. Media reports, however, have suggested friction between the Trump administration and Machado.

In interviews with Reuters and Axios, US administration officials have anonymously expressed frustration with the opposition leader’s repeated efforts to return home, particularly after a pair of deadly earthquakes in Venezuela last July.

Axios quoted one official as calling Machado’s push “political opportunism”.

Machado, however, remains one of the most popular figures in Venezuela’s opposition.

In October 2023, Machado won the opposition coalition’s presidential primary, but in January 2024, Venezuela’s courts blocked her from running in the upcoming race.

The courts upheld a 15-year ban on her holding public office, reportedly due to her support of US sanctions against the Maduro government.

Gonzalez ultimately replaced Machado as the opposition candidate in the 2024 race. Maduro claimed victory for a third term as Venezuela’s president in that election cycle, despite widespread criticism that the vote did not meet democratic standards.

The opposition released vote tallies that appeared to show Gonzalez had won the race.

The US had recognised Gonzalez as the country’s rightful president-elect and denied the legitimacy of Maduro’s election claims.

Machado was previously removed from the National Assembly in 2014, due to her activism against the Venezuelan government.

A third round of talks between the Rodriguez government and the opposition began in Venezuela this month.

But instead of including Machado, the negotiations have involved members of the 2015 National Assembly, which was led by the opposition and dissolved under Maduro.

Still, in a statement this month, the US State Department praised the talks as aiding the Venezuelan government’s reform.

“Political reconciliation talks between the interim Venezuelan government and 2015 National Assembly representatives are producing tangible reforms in civil liberties and political rights, laying the groundwork for credible elections and a democratic transition,” the State Department said.

articles.title: Japan's MMX mission set to grab a piece of Mars's moon Phobos
articles.summary: A spacecraft is set to launch on an ambitious mission to bring 10g of Martian moon dust back to Earth.
articles.body:
A space mission is set to launch on Monday that will attempt to grab a piece of Mars' moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth.

If it is successful, this will become the first time a sample has been returned from Mars or its moons to be analysed in laboratories here on Earth.

The spacecraft will blast off from Japan and arrive at Phobos in August 2027.

It is hoped that the Mars Moons Exploration (MMX) mission, which is led by the Japanese Space Agency, will solve the mystery of how Mars's moons formed.

Prof Sara Russell, from the Natural History Museum, who is the MMX mission's deputy for sample analysis, said: "There hasn't yet been a successful mission to go to Phobos and bring a bit back to Earth.

"I think this is an incredibly ambitious and fun mission," she said.

There are only three moons in the inner Solar System: our own Moon, and two around Mars, which are called Phobos and Deimos.

Both of these are tiny - Phobos is about 20km (12 miles) across and Deimos is about 10km (six miles) across. They are also irregularly shaped, looking a bit like space potatoes.

The MMX spacecraft will study Deimos as it arrives in the Mars neighbourhood, and then will focus on Phobos.

It plans to set down a small rover to explore the terrain, though this will be no easy feat.

Sara Russell says no one has ever landed a rover on such a small moon.

"The moon itself doesn't have very much of its own gravity," she explained.

"But it's next to an enormous planet that's got a much higher gravity, and that makes it much harder to get a rover onto the surface."

The rover will scout out a landing site so that the MMX spacecraft itself can later touch down on Phobos.

Once on the surface, it will deploy a robotic arm and two samplers to grab some moon dust.

This material will be packed into a small capsule that will return to Earth in 2031, landing in the Woomera desert of South Australia.

The amount of material that will come back is tiny - just 10g.

"It's a very small [amount] actually," said Dr Chrysa Avdellidou, from Leicester University, who is working with the Japanese mission.

"However we can do several studies even on individual grains… You don't need to have kilos back from a surface in order to do science. So it's worth every gram," she said.

Scientists believe the sample will finally shed light on the puzzle of where Mars's moons came from.

Either a space rock smashed into Mars early in its history, and Phobos and Deimos were created from the debris.

Or the moons are two wandering asteroids from the outer Solar System, which were grabbed by the Red Planet's gravity.

"When we get the sample back, we'll be able to look in detail at its chemistry and its mineral composition - and the two hypotheses will produce very distinct results," said Sara Russell.

"It should be pretty much immediately obvious.. whether it's the product of this dramatic impact or whether it's a captured asteroid. So we'll find that out really quickly."

The team is also hoping there might be an extra bonus coming back to their labs.

"One of the really exciting things is that Phobos is so close to the Mars surface that whenever there's an impact into the Mars surface, little grains might actually become implanted into Phobos itself," said Russell.

"And that means that the sample we get back may actually contain grains of Mars as well. So it can give us really direct information about the composition and history of Mars."

Bringing material from Mars back to Earth has long been an ambition of space scientists.

The Nasa Perseverance rover, which has been exploring Mars since 2021, has been carefully collecting samples on Mars and storing them in canisters.

But a second Nasa/ESA mission, called Mars Sample Return, that would have picked up and returned these canisters, has been effectively cancelled, after its funding was halted by the US Congress.

China is planning its own sampling mission to Mars, set to launch in 2028. It will attempt to return Martian material to Earth in 2031.

We do already have some fragments of the Red Planet here on Earth in the form of Martian meteorites.

These are pieces of Mars that were blasted off the surface by asteroid strikes, and ended up being hurled towards the Earth.

Martian meteorites are extremely rare, but like all space rocks that fall to our planet, they become contaminated as soon as they get here, mixing with the air, dust, soil and water.

Scientists are so desperate to get their gloved hands on a direct sample from Mars and its moons because it would be pristine.

The MMX mission is scheduled to blast off from the Tanegashima Space Center at 0441 local time on 20 October (2041BST 19 October).

articles.title: EU tariffs aimed at China hitting Ukraine, steel boss says
articles.summary: The boss of one of Ukraine's biggest steel companies says the country has been "bundled together" in measures aimed at curbing cheap imports.
articles.body:
The boss of one of Ukraine's biggest steel companies has called on the European Union to drop import restrictions on products made from the country, arguing it has been "bundled together" in measures aimed a curbing cheap imports from the likes of China.

Yuriy Ryzhenkov, chief executive of Metinvest, told the BBC the recently-imposed tariffs on imported steel to the EU were "unfair" and had been put in place "without any consideration for the situation Ukraine is in".

He said he wished to see "at least a carve out" for Ukraine to access the EU market.

A spokesperson for the European Commission said the EU "took into account the difficult situation" of Ukraine when deciding its steel policy.

The trading bloc has recently imposed restrictions on steel imports in an effort to protect steel manufacturers of member nations.

It has capped the amount of steel which can enter the EU tax free at 18.3 million tonnes per year - a 47% reduction from 2024 levels.

There are some country-specific quotas in the policy, but the overall aim is to cut the amount of steel that can be imported due to member nations struggling to compete with cheap imports from the likes of China and Turkey.

Despite a free-trade agreement (FTA) being in place between the EU and Ukraine, the FTA does not stop the EU from introducing separate trade protection measures.

"Ukraine has been bundled together into those measures without any consideration for the situation Ukraine is in," Ryzhenkov said, pointing to the war with Russia.

"Access to the European market is crucial for survival," he added. "The restrictive measures that have been put in place by the authorities in the European Union, they don't help.

"I think it's unfair that Ukraine has been treated in the same way as all of the other importers into the European Union."

The Ukraine steel industry estimates steel exports to the EU could ultimately fall by about 50–60%.

The EU said Ukraine's specific steel quota guaranteed exports of the metal, but acknowledged this was at a "level lower than in the past years".

"Despite the war effort, Ukraine remains an important exporter of steel to the EU," a spokesperson said, adding it had "offered compensations" to its largest suppliers, which included Ukraine.

Steel products are a foundation in Ukraine's economy. Before the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, metallurgy and mining accounted for roughly 10% of Ukraine's national income and a third of its exports. The EU is its top customer.

But the industry has suffered from the continued Russian bombardment.

All of Ukraine's steel mills have been bombed at points since the conflict began in 2022, but Ryzhenkov said strikes had "intensified significantly recently".

At one point in September, there was "no single tonne of steel produced" in Ukraine for the first time in about 150 years, he added.

Almost 800 Metinvest workers have been killed since the war began.

Ryzhenkov said the company had "improved the covered areas" at its mills where workers can shelter during air raids.

"The only thing we can do is to design procedures to keep people safe and just obey those procedures and try to minimise the risks."

"Unfortunately, you cannot cover a whole steel mill to avoid it being damaged."

Ryzhenkov said he expected the coming winter to be "one of the hardest in our history".

"We are in a dire situation when we don't have logistics to access any other market apart from the EU and cutting our available market by 60%, that doesn't help for the industry to survive."

articles.title: Congo’s fast-moving Ebola outbreak spreads to eighth province
articles.summary: The Health Ministry has recorded two cases, including one death, in Nord-Ubangi province. Both people were men in their 20s, the ministry said.
articles.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached an eighth province in the country’s north, authorities said on Sunday as the spread of the world’s fastest-growing outbreak of the disease on record continues to outpace response efforts. The Health Ministry has recorded two cases, including one death, in Nord-Ubangi province, bordering the Central African Republic. The ministry said both patients were men in their 20s living in the Wapinda health zone, which borders Bas-Uele province, where Ebola cases have been reported previously. Authorities have recorded at least 9,400 cases, including over 4,500 deaths, in the outbreak declared in mid-May, making it the deadliest in Congo’s history. The virus has spilled over into other countries including neighboring Uganda, which has since declared itself free of the disease, and Kenya, which recorded an eighth case on Sunday. The Central African Republic has not recorded any confirmed cases. “We see pockets of Ebola generally going down, but unfortunately geographically it’s spreading out,” World Health Organization Regional Director for Africa Mohamed Yakub Janabi told The Associated Press in an interview in Beni, eastern Congo, on Friday. Janabi said one of the biggest challenges has been convincing those who are infected to seek medical assistance, adding that some deaths occur in the community outside of health centers. Serge Ngalebato, epidemiologist and field coordinator for the Wamba health zone in Haut-Uele province, told the AP health workers in his health zone introduced periodic home visits because people were too afraid to go to a hospital. Nord-Ubangi is located between Sud-Ubangi and Bas-Uele, the last two provinces the disease had spread to along the border with the Central African Republic, where recurring armed violence has forced thousands to flee and take refuge in Congolese border communities. Access in the region can be difficult due to poor roads and limited communication networks. Ituri province in eastern Congo remains the disease's epicenter, accounting for almost three quarters of confirmed cases, according to the government’s most recent data, which shows 66 health zones have been affected since the start of the outbreak. Congo's state news agency ACP reported Sunday that authorities in North Kivu province — where WHO says substantial transmission continues — will introduce a one-week ban from Monday on people entering the province from Ituri in an effort to slow the spread of the virus. Other measures that will be introduced include prohibiting carrying more than two people on a motorcycle or four people in a car, as well as suspending big public gatherings such as at mass sports activities, nightclubs and political demonstrations. The spread of the outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment, is fueled by mass population movements, rebel violence, mistrust and poor working conditions of front-line workers. Ngalebato said efforts to contain the virus in the Wamba health zone were initially met with resistance among local residents, but as time went on the community became more understanding and began reporting positive cases. “Ebola is a community disease. If the community does not cooperate, it will be very difficult,” he said. He added most of the cases reported in his health zone are around mining areas where the population moves constantly, so a lot of deaths were reported in these areas.

articles.title: Flight from Israel makes emergency landing in Bulgaria after bomb threat
articles.summary: Crew of Austrian Airlines flight OS82 decides to land in Sofia after receiving bomb threat, Bulgarian authorities say.
articles.body:
An Airbus A320 flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna has made an emergency landing in Bulgaria following a reported bomb threat, according to the Bulgarian Ministry of Transport.

Austrian Airlines flight OS82 was near the border with Romania when the crew received a bomb threat and decided to land in the Bulgarian capital, Sofia, the Transport Ministry said in a statement on Sunday.

Bulgaria’s Ministry of Defence said an air force MiG-29 fighter jet escorted the plane to Sofia airport.

Initial information showed the aircraft carried six crew members and 51 passengers, all of whom have all since disembarked, according to the Transport Ministry’s statement.

The airline told the AFP news agency that a security search of the aircraft was conducted.

“Once the search of the aircraft is complete, the passengers will be rebooked onto alternative flights as quickly as possible,” the airline said.

A crisis response team has been set up, and relevant authorities have launched an investigation into the incident, the Bulgarian Transport Ministry said.

According to aviation and flight tracking site FlightAware, Austrian Airlines 82 left the Ben Gurion airport in Tel Aviv on Sunday at 6:46pm local time (15:46 GMT) and landed about three hours later at Vasil Levski airport in Sofia at 9:43pm (18:43 GMT).

Flightradar24 data showed it entered Romanian airspace at about 9:10pm (18:10 GMT) before turning south and heading back towards Bulgaria.

Information from the flight-tracking platform ADS-B Exchange indicates the aircraft was transmitting squawk code 7700 – a signal for a general emergency – at around the same time.

Last month, a Flydubai plane carrying 174 passengers was on its way from the United Arab Emirates to Tel Aviv when a co-pilot allegedly attacked the pilot with an axe in an attempt to crash the plane.

The aircraft plunged about 17,000 feet (5,180 metres) before it was brought back under control by other Flydubai pilots after passengers and other crew subdued the alleged attacker.

The flight was diverted and forced to make an emergency landing at Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Tabuk, northwestern Saudi Arabia.

Authorities in the UAE said the co-pilot was on a “suicide” mission to crash the plane at Israel’s Ben Gurion airport in Tel Aviv.

The co-pilot, Hamam Al-Hammami , an Omani national, has since been charged with terrorism offences in the UAE.

The Israeli government responded to the incident by ordering checks on the identities of all pilots flying into the country.

articles.title: Dia do Piauí com bate e volta: veja lista de 5 passeios rápidos | G1
articles.standfirst: Roteiros incluem cachoeiras, cânions e trilhas a até 300 km da capital; empresário do setor, engenheiro e praticante de ecoturismo relatam rotas, custos e desafios de acesso a pontos turísticos do estado.
articles.summary: Roteiros incluem cachoeiras, cânions e trilhas a até 300 km da capital; empresário do setor, engenheiro e praticante de ecoturismo relatam rotas, custos e desafios de acesso.
articles.body:
Bate e Volta no Piauí: veja lista de passeios rápidos saindo da capital — Foto: Montagem g1

Nesta segunda-feira (19), feriado em que se celebra o Dia do Piauí, opções de turismo de aventura e ecoturismo pelo interior do estado atraem turistas que buscam alternativas às praias do litoral e à rotina urbana.

Para mapear os principais destinos e entender a logística dessas viagens, o g1 conversou com um empresário do setor de transportes turísticos, um engenheiro ambiental e uma comerciante adeptos das trilhas e acampamentos regionais.

Do transporte de passageiros ao ecoturismo

O empresário Airton Cézar Nogueira de Carvalho trabalha há mais de 30 anos com transporte de passageiros. Antes de abrir o próprio negócio, atuou por quase cinco anos na entrega de panfletos para agências de turismo e, com o dinheiro que economizou, comprou o primeiro veículo para iniciar os serviços de fretamento e passeios.

Segundo Airton Cézar, os roteiros oferecidos são voltados principalmente para atividades em áreas de vegetação, como acampamentos e banhos de cachoeira. Por isso, os passeios não têm foco em hospedagem em hotéis ou em pacotes turísticos convencionais.

Cézar destacou a importância da parceria com moradores locais para a condução dos grupos.

"Em todos os locais que visitamos, contratamos um guia da própria região. Além de ser uma questão de segurança, ajuda a movimentar a economia local", afirmou o empresário.

Com base nos depoimentos dos entrevistados, o g1 reuniu os principais pontos turísticos indicados para visitação no estado:

Riacho Santa Bárbara ( Monsenhor Gil / Beneditinos )

Acesso recomendado : Por Monsenhor Gil (rodovia BR-316 e vias secundárias), devido às condições de trafegabilidade.

O que fazer : Banhos em águas cristalinas perenes e passeio de caiaque.

Custos : Passeios bate e volta custam em média R$ 130 por pessoa (transporte de van e caiaque inclusos).

Camping e Hospedagem : Há áreas ao ar livre e apoio de chácaras locais para acampamento. Para hospedagem convencional, a estrutura mais próxima fica na zona urbana de Monsenhor Gil.

Cachoeira das Arraias ( Castelo do Piauí )

Cachoeira das Arraias — Foto: Reprodução /TV Clube

O que fazer : Banhos em duas quedas d'água principais (de 15 a 20 metros no período de chuvas), piscinas naturais e caminhadas ecológicas no Parque Municipal da Pedra do Castelo.

Custos : Entrada gratuita; recomenda-se a contratação de guia local.

Camping e Hospedagem : Há espaços para acampamento de dia ou pernoite autorizados no entorno do parque. Pousadas e hotéis funcionam no centro de Castelo do Piauí.

Cânion do Esporão — Foto: Cézar Transportes

Distância de Teresina : Aproximadamente 195 km.

O que fazer : Banho nas águas do Rio São Miguel, trilhas em vegetação preservada e contemplação de formações rochosas.

Custos : Varia conforme o transporte e contratação de condutor local.

Camping e Hospedagem : Áreas adequadas para acampamento de grupos. Hospedagem urbana disponível em Castelo do Piauí.

Cânion do Rio Poti ( Buriti dos Montes / Castelo do Piauí)

Cânion do Rio Poti — Foto: Micheli Brito

Distância de Teresina : Aproximadamente 230 km.

O que fazer : Passeios de barco de grande porte, remada de caiaque, observação de fendas rochosas e registros rupestres.

Custos : Passeios guiados de caiaque e apoio de embarcação variam conforme o pacote comercial contratado com empresas credenciadas. A partir de R$ 350.

Camping e Hospedagem : Permite acampamento às margens do rio ou em áreas de apoio rural. Opções de hotéis e pousadas encontram-se no centro urbano de Castelo do Piauí (a cerca de 40 km do cânion) ou em Buriti dos Montes.

Capadócia Piauiense ( São José do Piauí / São João da Canabrava )

Capadócia Nordestina — Foto: Josielton Rodrigues

Distância de Teresina : Cerca de 296 km.

O que fazer : Trilhas entre formações rochosas e observação do céu noturno.

Custos : Acesso gratuito, variando os custos conforme o transporte e guia contratado.

Camping e Hospedagem : O local possui espaço amplo para armação de barracas em pontos de apoio de moradores regionais. Pousadas e hotéis estão disponíveis nos municípios de Picos e São José do Piauí.

Trecho de Caiaque entre Barra Grande e Macapá — Foto: Cézar Transportes

O que fazer : Remada em manguezais e braços de mar, com observação da fauna marinha e da costa piauiense.

Custos : Pacotes de fim de semana (saída na sexta-feira à noite e retorno no domingo) custam cerca de R$ 390 por pessoa, incluindo transporte de van, aluguel de casa de apoio e acompanhamento de guia.

Camping e Hospedagem : O litoral dispõe de áreas de camping estruturadas, pousadas e casas de temporada para aluguel.

Parques Nacionais Serra da Capivara e Serra das Confusões ( São Raimundo Nonato / Caracol )

Serra das Confusões — Foto: Micheli Brito

Distância de Teresina : 530 km (São Raimundo Nonato) e 600 km (Caracol).

O que fazer : Visitação a sítios arqueológicos, observação da caatinga e caminhadas por formações rochosas.

Custos : Taxas de condutores credenciados pelos parques variam conforme o tamanho do grupo e o circuito escolhido.

Camping e Hospedagem : Estruturas de camping e pousadas comunitárias em vilarejos próximos às entradas dos parques (como Coronel José Dias e Caracol), além de hotéis em São Raimundo Nonato.

Cânion dos Vianas — Foto: Cézar Transportes

O que fazer : Expedições off-road em veículos 4x4, quadriciclos, ciclismo, caminhadas entre paredões de até 100 metros de altura e visitação a grutas e pinturas rupestres.

Custos : Exige veículo tracionado ou contratação de serviço especializado local. Valor varia com a empresa.

Camping e Hospedagem : O percurso é próprio para acampamento selvagem estruturado por expedições. A rede hoteleira mais próxima situa-se na cidade de Bom Jesus.

O engenheiro ambiental José Ruthênio Júnior contou que a prática de percorrer o interior começou na infância. Entre os trajetos realizados no estado, ele destacou a expedição de seis dias feita em 2021 passando pela Capadócia Piauiense, Serra da Capivara, Serra das Confusões e Cânion dos Vianas.

O engenheiro relembro também uma ocasião em 2017, durante um acampamento no Cânion do Rio Poti, em que avistou uma onça-parda na margem oposta do rio durante a noite.

"O animal estava bebendo água do outro lado da margem, a cerca de 30 metros de distância. Mantivemos a calma e retornamos devagar para o acampamento", relatou.

Para quem busca iniciar no ecoturismo, a comerciante Micheli Brito recomenda começar por pontos mais próximos e consolidados, como o Cânion do Poti. Ela enfatizou a necessidade de planejamento e itens básicos para as caminhadas:

Uso de garrafa de água para hidratação constante;

Alimentos leves para consumo durante o trajeto;

Recolhimento de todo o lixo gerado durante a visita.

Os entrevistados também comentaram sobre a falta de acessibilidade rodoviária como uma das principais dificuldades para a expansão do turismo no Piauí. Segundo Cézar, muitas cachoeiras e atrações do estado exigem caminhadas de 6 a 7 km em mata fechada por falta de vias trafegáveis para veículos comuns.

"O estado possui muitos pontos com potencial turístico, mas a falta de estradas trafegáveis impede que o visitante chegue aos locais. Onde o asfalto ou o acesso melhorou, como no Cânion do Poti, o fluxo de turistas aumentou consideravelmente", concluiu o empresário.

articles.title: GTA 6: Can you cheat on someone with a video game character?
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI lets you build and nurture a romantic relationship but some say dates with a fictional character are a step too far.
articles.body:
Imagine your partner spending hours flirting with someone else, trying to hold their hand and taking them on dates. Most people would have questions.

But what if that someone only exists inside a video game?

The latest instalment in Rockstar's blockbuster Grand Theft Auto franchise is set to be the biggest entertainment launch of the year when it is released next month.

Judging by previews, the connection between its two main characters is a central feature.

Rockstar has hinted that the Bonnie and Clyde-type protagonists Jason and Lucia do not have to become a full-on romantic couple.

But their relationship can grow by spending time together outside of the main crime and life-on-the-run storyline – through shopping, visiting bars and restaurants and working out together.

Smaller interactions like holding hands and quickly responding to each other's texts can help build a bond.

The idea has restarted a debate almost as old as gaming itself: if you are that invested in a fictional relationship, is your real-life partner entitled to be upset?

In September, polling company YouGov put that question to more than 4,000 British adults.

About 6% said they would regard it as cheating, while a further 19% said they would "not be okay with it". Women were considerably more likely than men to take a dim view.

Alli Franco, a 30-year-old Texan who posts anime and gaming content to more than a million followers on TikTok, says she felt "dismayed" watching the debate unfold online.

"If your partner is insecure about a fictional character, then there needs to be some serious reflection," she told the BBC.

"It's similar to having a crush on a TV star, but even further removed from cheating since there is no other actual person involved.”

After Franco posted a video on the subject, hundreds of commenters appeared to agree with her, although some did have reservations.

"To be honest, it depends," wrote one. "If you're cancelling plans with your significant other or directing your intimacy towards a fictional character, then that is a little odd."

For decades, video games have allowed players to build relationships with non-player characters, or NPCs.

Gamers could marry villagers in Harvest Moon in 1996, shape emotional storylines in Final Fantasy VII and pursue more complex romances in role-playing games like Baldur's Gate II.

In life simulator The Sims, they could flirt, date, marry and have children with computer-controlled characters.

But all those interactions were tightly scripted, based on rules and storylines written in advance by game developers.

GTA 6 appears to offer something more dynamic, allowing players to shape the relationship between Jason and Lucia through a wider range of open-world interactions and choices.

"The more sophisticated games get, the less likely it is that players get pulled out of the experience," says Arienne Ferchaud, an associate professor at Florida State University who studies how people form connections with fictional characters.

"Games are doing a better job of mimicking reality and mimicking social relationships."

Grand Theft Auto 6 may represent the current cutting edge of game design, but the next leap forward could come from artificial intelligence.

Nvidia, Ubisoft and other huge tech companies are already experimenting with generative AI systems that allow players to hold more natural conversations with NPCs.

Future characters could remember past encounters, react to a player's actions and build relationships that change over time rather than following a pre-written script.

Ferchaud believes that could make games feel even more immersive.

"You could have relationships that feel more solid or more special," she says, although she argues AI as it exists today would still be creating "a stronger illusion" rather than a genuinely meaningful connection.

Whether that is exciting or unsettling may depend on the player, and there has been some resistance to the wider use of the technology in gaming .

Franco says she is already seeing adverts for AI chatbots that let fans talk to their favourite anime characters.

"I can definitely see AI integrating into games and making it a more realistic experience," she says.

"But should that happen I would still see it as just a game. At the end of the day you can't cheat with lines of code."

articles.title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine
articles.summary:
Antisocial behaviour on buses in England could lead to fines while a new campaign is also being launched for trains.
A national campaign asking rail passengers "share the carriage, not the noise" is being launched.
articles.body:
Passengers who play loud music on buses in England could be fined up to £100 under an attempt by the government to crack down on antisocial behaviour.

The measures also seek to tackle littering, vaping and threatening behaviour to help improve journeys on all forms of public transport.

Offenders on buses could be issued with the fines under new powers for local authorities.

A national campaign asking rail passengers "share the carriage, not the noise" is also being launched. The proposed crackdown has been welcomed by campaigners, but some have questioned how it can be enforced.

"We've all been on the train when someone starts blasting music or videos from their phone. It gets on your nerves and can quickly spoil the journey," said Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

Under existing powers, those who are asked to stop and refuse could be removed from a train or fined up to £1,000.

The phenomenon has been given many terms - including loudcasting or sodcasting - and in recent years, Ofcom, YouGov and Transport for London (TfL) have all published polls showing the vast majority of people dislike it.

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said small changes in behaviour "can make a massive difference to people's experience on public transport".

The government said it had issued new guidance to local authorities on powers - which were introduced earlier this year - to help them crackdown on loud music and other antisocial behaviour on buses in England.

These new powers allow them to impose new rules on buses, but still need to be signed off by the Transport Secretary

Those who commit offences could face fixed penalties of up to £100.

The government says bus drivers will not be responsible for enforcing the new rules. It says authorised officers, including Transport Safety Officers and the Police, will deal with the incidents.

Meanwhile a new national campaign aims to remind rail passengers to "share the carriage, not the noise", to improve journeys for everyone

The campaign will be launched across operator websites, social media, and in carriages. The government said this would end the current "patchwork" of approaches across different rail operators, and help create "a clear, consistent message across the network".

The general secretary of the TSSA transport union, Maryam Eslamdoust, said tackling antisocial behaviour on public transport was "a step in the right direction".

However, she added that the government must also "urgently confront the violence, threats and abuse faced by passengers and transport workers".

"Increasing the budget for British Transport Police is vital to protect people, respond to incidents and bring violent offenders to justice," she said.

Michael Solomon Williams from the Campaign for Better Transport told the BBC antisocial behaviour could be a "real deterrent" to people using public transport, especially those with different accessibility needs.

He also questioned how the new measures will be enforced. "When local authorities are required to do the enforcement there are perhaps some question marks about how a local police force might be called upon on bus services, for example, where we don't tend to see British Transport Police."

Richard Holden MP, Shadow Transport Secretary, said: "After we led the charge against antisocial behaviour on public transport last summer, Ministers have worked out that nobody wants to endure pounding techno or blaring hip hop on a packed train or bus.

"But passengers and railway staff face far more serious problems. Assaults against rail staff have risen by 68%, while prosecutions have slumped under Labour. It's time for Andy Burnham to get serious about enforcement, tackling violence and protecting those who work on our railways."

Liberal Democrat Transport spokesperson, Olly Glover MP said: "Tough talk means nothing without enforcement.

"Unless the Government funds transport safety officers on the ground, these new rules won't be worth the paper they're printed on."

Independent watchdog Transport Focus said research it had published in June showed personal safety and security was now fundamental to passengers' confidence in the railway.

"Four in 10 passengers say that anti-social behaviour has made them feel vulnerable when travelling," said Alex Campbell, Transport Focus's director of policy and insight.

"Measures that reduce nuisance behaviour, such as playing loud music and vaping, can help improve people's experience and encourage more people to choose public transport."

articles.title: Ohio State QB Julian Sayin's injury may completely reshape the College Football Playoff race
articles.summary: Julian Sayin's shoulder injury could reshape the college football playoff picture as Ohio State faces a brutal schedule with true freshman Luke Fahey.
articles.body: It was a stunning week seven in the world of college football, both for the number of top programs that lost, and for who they lost to. BYU took down Notre Dame, with a little help from yet another controversial last-second game clock issue. Auburn beat the heavily favored Georgia Bulldogs in Athens. Florida rose from the dead to upset Texas in Austin on the back of another disappointing performance from Arch Manning. Tennessee had a big home win over Alabama, holding the powerful Crimson Tide offense to just 10 points. Miami held on to beat Florida State thanks to some questionable officiating, but just not losing bumped the Hurricanes up to No. 1. But arguably the most impactful win of the weekend was The Ohio State Buckeyes ending Indiana's 22-game winning streak in Bloomington. With around a minute remaining, Indiana seemed to tie it when Josh Hoover hit a wide open Nick Marsh in the end zone. Marsh's foot came down just out of bounds, however, and Ohio State hung on to the 19-15 win. WEEK 7 AP TOP 25 POLL FEATURES A COMPLETE SHUFFLE AFTER CHAOTIC WEEKEND, WITH MIAMI TAKING OVER THE TOP SPOT Thanks to the 12-team playoff, the win for OSU and loss for Indiana wouldn't typically mean either team is out of the running. And this week's AP Top 25 Poll reflects that; Ohio State is No. 3, and Indiana is No. 5, thanks to the carnage around them. So how could it be the most impactful? Because of what happened to starting quarterback Julian Sayin's shoulder in the fourth quarter. Indiana defensive lineman Mario Landino sacked Sayin in the fourth quarter, forcing a fumble and the injury when he hit the ground. The 21-year-old junior immediately could be seen favoring his right arm and went to the locker room, emerging a few minutes afterward with his arm in a sling. After the game, head coach Ryan Day was light on specifics, saying he didn't have further details on what exactly the injury was, but did admit that Sayin's likely to miss "several weeks." Day was adamant that true freshman backup Luke Fahey would be able to step in, particularly with a bye week approaching. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "We'll regroup," he said. "We've got a good team. When Luke's in there, we just may need to do things just a little bit differently, but the bye week gives us a chance to regroup on that and put our heads together." After replacing Sayin, Fahey went 0-2 passing, though he did draw a penalty that helped extend a Buckeyes' drive. The bye week reps will help, but as a true freshman, Fahey's light on college experience and now thrust into the starting role at a pivotal time. Which is why Sayin's injury could reshape the playoff picture. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Though OSU has the bye week coming up, their next game is on the road against the No. 16 USC Trojans. With Sayin, the Buckeyes would be sizable favorites. With a true freshman backup? The calculus might change significantly. The SC defense isn't Indiana, but making your first career start, on the road, in front of what's sure to be a sold-out, hostile LA Coliseum crowd, against a team hungry to make statement and reach the College Football Playoff for the first time in Lincoln Riley's tenure? It's not ideal, to say the least. If Sayin isn't able to return after SC, the Buckeyes return home to face ... Oregon. While that matchup no longer looks like the battle of top-5 teams it looked like in the preseason, the Ducks' defense is still extremely talented, and even with their backup QB's, pulled out an impressive win against a very good Nebraska team. The schedule doesn't get much easier after that either. Ranked Northwestern comes to Columbus. Then the Buckeyes travel to Lincoln to play Nebraska, and host Michigan in "The Game." USC is on the playoff bubble, but if the Trojans beat Wisconsin and OSU, now with Fahey playing, they'd immediately move into the top-10. A slip up at home against a still dangerous Oregon team, and the Buckeyes could suddenly be on the outside of the top-12 looking in. Or maybe Iowa, considering the Hawkeyes' relatively favorable closing schedule compared to other top programs in the two superconferences. There's a long way to go, with nearly half the season's games left to be played. Ohio State could still beat USC on the road, even with a backup, considering the Trojans' struggles to win big games under Riley and their suffocating defense. Sayin could also return by the first week of November, with OSU staying on track to go to the Big Ten Championship Game. But there are suddenly a lot more variables for the Buckeyes than it looked like. In a year where any and all teams seem beatable, by anyone, Ohio State heads into games against USC and Oregon with a true freshman quarterback. articles.title: UK Weather: Stormy weather possible as jet stream roars to life
articles.summary: Gales are possible later this week as a deep low pressure system crosses the UK, but uncertainty remains whether impacts will be enough for it to be a named storm.
articles.body:
The UK may see its first named storm of the autumn as forecasts show the potential for a deep area of low pressure to cross the UK later this week.

A strengthening jet stream triggered by temperature contrasts across North America will cause turbulent conditions to develop.

All areas will experience rain at times, including those currently in drought, but amounts of rain will depend on the exact track of a stormy low pressure system later in the week.

After a chilly weekend, temperatures will generally remain slightly below average for mid-October.

Autumn has been relatively calm in many areas with little in the way of disruptive weather and rainfall has remained deficient across a huge swathe of England and Wales.

Parts of Herefordshire have seen only a tenth of the rainfall typically expected by this stage of October, and the dry conditions persist for much of England. The Environment Agency recently declared severe drought for parts of southern England.

This month continues the warming trend we have seen so far this year, with mean temperatures - which is an average of maximum and minimum temperature - between 1 and 3 Celsius above normal for October.

Over the weekend, all four nations saw their lowest temperature of autumn so far. Parts of Scotland and Northern Ireland dropped to minus 4 Celsius on Sunday morning with minus 2 Celsius recorded in northern England while Wales registered its first air frost of the season.

Strong jet stream to bring turbulent weather

After a frosty start in Scotland and Northern Ireland on Monday it will turn more cloudy. Overnight rain in England and Wales will largely die out and skies will brighten.

It should be a slightly milder to start the week.

Expect cloudy skies on Tuesday with rain developing again in England, Wales and Scotland. Northern Ireland may be dry with some sunshine, before another band of rain arrives from the Atlantic by the end of the day.

Bands of rain will move across the UK on Wednesday before the weather takes a turn for the worst in some areas at the end of the week.

Weather models suggest there is the potential for the jet stream to guide a deep area of low pressure across the UK by Friday.

In addition to heavy rain, gales or even severe gales will be wrapped around the deep low.

At the moment most computer models take the centre of the low pressure system across the south of the UK. The highest risk of disruptive winds would be over southernmost parts of England and Wales and possibly some eastern coastal counties of England later on Friday. Such a track would leave Scotland and parts of Northern Ireland with quieter weather conditions.

However, some computer models show the deep low taking a more northerly track. If this happens, then gales and disruption could be expected more widely with impacts also in Scotland and Northern Ireland.

The uncertainty of the track means the forecast could change and it is important to keep across any potential Met Office weather warnings .

Will the UK see the first named storm of the season?

The UK storm season runs from September until August and it is not unusual to reach this stage of autumn without any named storms.

If the UK Met Office or Ireland's Met Éireann expect this week's low pressure system to bring significant impacts, that would lead them to issue weather warnings at an amber level or higher . If the storm is then named, it will be called 'Storm Austen'.

It is possible that the low pressure system could follow an even more southerly track, meaning greater impacts in France and less across the UK, and the French weather service MeteoFrance could name it 'Storm Bruna'.

Developments at the end of the week will also dictate potential weather conditions into the following week, with some computer models showing further stormy weather at times, while others suggest quieter conditions under a developing high pressure system.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia on edge: Iconic Kingdom Centre sends workers home amid Houthi attacks
articles.summary: Kingdom Centre in Riyadh ordered all office employees to work remotely as Iran-backed Houthi missile and drone attacks rattled Saudi Arabia.
articles.body: One of Saudi Arabia’s most iconic skyscrapers ordered office workers to stay home Sunday as escalating attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels rattled the capital of Riyadh amid fears of a widening Middle East conflict. The move came after the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two drones in the Riyadh area, a third over the Eastern Province and two ballistic missiles in southern Saudi Arabia overnight, after authorities had earlier issued a threat alert in the capital, also shared on X. Management at the 99-story Kingdom Centre, a landmark on Riyadh's skyline, ordered office employees to work remotely until further notice, according to reporting by Agence France-Presse (AFP). The directive affects a building whose tenants include major international financial institutions such as Merrill Lynch, consulting giant McKinsey & Company and the International Monetary Fund. THE HOUTHIS AREN'T SOMEBODY ELSE'S PROBLEM. AMERICA CAN'T AFFORD TO LOOK AWAY "Please be advised that remote working arrangements are mandatory for all office employees at Kingdom Centre, effective immediately and until further notice," building management said in an email obtained by AFP. Employees were instructed not to report back to their offices. The shopping mall at the base of the tower, however, remained open to the public. Management did not specify a reason for the directive, but it came as repeated missile and drone attacks by Yemen's Houthis disrupted the Saudi capital. The security concerns also follow a deadly Oct. 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 others. As previously reported by Fox News Digital, another strike the following day killed one person and injured 11. Airport operations have been severely disrupted, while schools in Riyadh have extended remote learning measures amid continued security threats. SAUDI ARABIA FACING 'BIGGEST THREAT' EVER TO OIL PRODUCTION AS IRAN-PROXY HOUTHIS LAUNCH ATTACKS, EXPERT SAYS The mounting crisis comes as Saudi Arabia's military reported two deaths in a helicopter crash near its southern border with Yemen. Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki, spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition, said Sunday that an AH-6i reconnaissance helicopter crashed in the Najran region because of a technical malfunction, killing both crew members. Saudi civil defense authorities also reported Sunday that six people were injured when a hostile projectile struck a residential neighborhood in Najran, damaging three homes and three vehicles. Meanwhile, Egypt moved toward potentially providing military assistance to Saudi Arabia as the kingdom confronts the growing Houthi threat. Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sissi requested an emergency parliamentary session to authorize defensive military support for Saudi Arabia if requested by Riyadh, Reuters reported. Lawmakers were expected to continue discussions Monday. NEW RISK FOR US CONSUMERS AS IRAN-BACKED ATTACKS THREATEN A SECOND MAJOR OIL CHOKEPOINT The Egyptian presidency said Cairo was prepared to provide Saudi Arabia with necessary support to defend its security, stability, territorial integrity and Islamic holy sites. articles.title: California woman indicted on charges she was spying for China
articles.summary: Federal prosecutors said Wanying Zhang was spying on a son of Taiwan’s president.
articles.body: A California woman who prosecutors allege was spying on a son of Taiwan’s president was indicted this month on charges of conspiracy and being an unregistered foreign agent for China. The indictment was filed Oct. 9 in U.S. District Court for the Central District of California, and the allegations it lays out mirror an earlier criminal complaint against the woman, Wanying Zhang, 34, of Irvine. Prosecutors say Zhang, who also goes by Heather, spied on a son of Taiwan’s president outside his home in the Seattle area at the behest of Chinese officials. The spying is alleged to have taken place between roughly June and September 2025, prosecutors claim. Taiwan is a self-ruled democracy that is the source of 90% of the world’s “leading-edge chip manufacturing,” according to the U.S. International Trade Administration. China claims Taiwan, which the U.S. has no official relationship with, though it is required by law to ensure Taiwan can defend itself. Prosecutors allege Zhang was under the direction of an unnamed Chinese government official and former classmate at her alma mater, China’s University of International Relations, which is “closely affiliated with China’s intelligence apparatus,” an FBI investigator said in earlier court documents. An example of the alleged activity was a request by the former classmate to send him pictures “of the house” where the son lives, according to the indictment. Prosecutors alleged that Zhang flew from California to Las Vegas and then to the Seattle area to conduct surveillance of the unidentified son and his home from outside. The indictment alleges she captured photos, video and license plate information and sent them to the person alleged to be her Chinese handler. An unidentified person, who had fled to China in September, was with her, prosecutors said. Zhang also traveled to China in August 2025 to meet with a Chinese government official, returned days later and told the official she would most likely be going to where the victim was the following week, according to the indictment. Her lawyer, Craig Harbaugh, did not immediately respond to a request for comment Sunday. Previously, Harbaugh, a veteran criminal defense attorney, described Zhang as an upstanding resident of Irvine, about 42 miles southeast of Los Angeles, where she lives with her husband and two young daughters. “The government’s theory — she’s been a sleeper agent for the last 10 years, working as a real estate agent, raising her family and will choose to go to China and abandon her work, her family and her home — it’s not supported,” Harbaugh said in court Oct. 7. The Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment late Sunday. Guo Jiakun, a spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Affairs Ministry, said this month after Zhang was arrested at Los Angeles International Airport that he was “not familiar” with the situation and that Beijing “opposes vilifying China by peddling the so-called ‘Chinese spy’ narrative.” U.S. Magistrate Judge Steve Kim ordered Zhang held in pretrial detention after prosecutors argued she poses a flight risk. The U.S. Bureau of Prisons website shows that she remains in custody. Zhang is scheduled to appear in federal district court Friday for a post-indictment arraignment. She could face up to 15 years in prison.

articles.title: Kenya confirms eighth Ebola case amid widening regional outbreak
articles.summary: Kenyan health authorities say latest patient was likely exposed to the country’s first Ebola case.
articles.body:
Kenyan health authorities say an eighth Ebola case has been detected in the East African nation.

Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth told Kenya’s Citizen TV that of the 38 people tested on Sunday, one had returned a positive result.

“He is a 49-year-old man who is not a healthcare worker. He developed fever, headache and muscle pain,” he said.

Amoth said the man, who worked as a patient attendant cleaning utensils and linens, was likely exposed to Kenya’s first Ebola case, discovered earlier this month.

He developed symptoms on Saturday, was quarantined and tested for the virus, a Ministry of Health source said.

The ministry reported four new cases on Saturday , three of whom were health workers who treated the country’s first Ebola patient, a man who travelled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) to Nairobi and died at a Nairobi hospital on October 5.

In a post on X, the ministry said the fourth person was related to the deceased patient.

Kenya has been on heightened alert, as the Ebola outbreak has spilled across the border from the DRC. The current outbreak is of the Bundibugyo strain of the virus, for which there is no vaccine or specific treatment.

The DRC has recorded at least 9,400 cases, including more than 4,500 deaths, in the deadliest outbreak in the country’s history, which started in May.

Ituri province in eastern DRC remains the disease’s epicentre, accounting for almost three quarters of confirmed cases, according to the government’s most recent data. It announced on Sunday that the virus has reached an eighth province, North Ubangi.

State-run news agency ACP reported on Sunday that authorities in North Kivu province, where the World Health Organization said substantial transmission continues, are introducing a one-week ban from Monday on people entering the province from Ituri in an effort to slow the spread.

Other measures set to be introduced include restrictions on passenger numbers in cars and on motorbikes and suspension of large public gatherings.

Neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 confirmed cases, including 15 imported from the DRC, and two deaths, before it was declared Ebola-free in August.

articles.title: Jordon Steele-John: Australian senator denies claims of misconduct against women
articles.summary: Jordon Steele-John says the timing of the claims is motivated by "nasty political games" within the Greens.
articles.body:
An Australian Greens senator has denied allegations of inappropriate behaviour towards women and accused his party of "nasty political games", days after the claims emerged.

Last Thursday, Greens leader David Shoebridge said Senator Jordon Steele-John, 32, had taken leave from the party room after a letter from seven current and former members said he had been accused of "multiple allegations" of misconduct between 2017 and 2025.

In an online post on Sunday, the senator denied the claims and said he was not on leave. On a sexual assault claim, he said police investigating the matter had closed the case and no charges were laid.

An internal party probe has been launched into the allegations.

Steele-John, who has cerebral palsy and uses a wheelchair, was first elected to the senate in Western Australia in November 2017.

In his letter responding to the claims, Steele-John said his nickname - "Feels on wheels" - initially referred to him being emotional when advocating for disability rights but had since taken on a "more sinister meaning" about his alleged mistreatment of women.

He accused Shoebridge of mishandling the matter and questioned the timing of the letter, saying "it is no coincidence" that the allegations were sent to the leader "the day after we agreed on the timeline for the next preselection" ahead of the next federal election.

Days after the letter with the claims was sent to Shoebridge, local media reported that the party had created a 47-page dossier years earlier that listed a number of allegations against Steele-John and how to manage media coverage if they emerged.

Steele-John said the dossier was made so that the media would not "bombard" the two women at the centre of those claims and that neither woman had made a complaint.

He acknowledged the allegations against him would have "damaged" the public's trust in him and said he was "committed to rebuilding that by acting with as much transparency and accountability as I can".

Shoebridge's office confirmed that the allegations had been referred to the Independent Parliamentary Standards Commission.

articles.title: Burnham warns of Neets-fuelled 'economic catastrophe and moral failure'
articles.summary: The UK faces "economic catastrophe" with one million young people not in work or training, the prime minister says.
articles.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has warned the UK faces an "economic catastrophe and moral failure" due to the nearly one million young people not in education, employment or training.

Writing in the Times newspaper , Burnham has laid out his case for the government to "invest in the success of our young people" rather than "pay for failure through the benefits system".

"Benefits will become the backstop, not the starting point," Burnham wrote in his piece published in Monday's paper.

Later this week, the government is expected to announce plans to give young people thousands of job opportunities. The Conservative Party has labelled the government's youth employment strategy "a disaster".

According to the latest data from the Office for National Statistics, there are almost a million people aged 16 to 24 known as Neets - not in education, employment or training.

In his opinion column, the prime minister said this reflected a "generation being denied its chance to get on in life".

"This is an economic catastrophe and a moral failure. And it must change," he wrote.

Burnham said two years of Covid lockdowns, social media that erodes "confidence and sense of belonging", an education system focused on the "university route", job markets with "too few opportunities" and failures of previous governments have all contributed to the Neets crisis.

"Today, the welfare system provides an assessment, a payment and, after that, goodbye," Burnham wrote. "Too often there is no support, no offer of skills and no opportunity to get a job."

He flagged a shift in the approach to welfare, which he said "will no longer begin by establishing which benefits a young person is entitled to" but rather "begin with their ambitions and the help they need to achieve them".

The prime minister added: "The safety net will always be there for those who cannot work. But if someone can work with the right help, the government has a duty to do everything in its power to make that happen."

Ministers are this week set to release plans for tens of thousands of new youth apprenticeships and placements in the construction industry, and at accounting, consulting and legal firms.

Shadow Business and Trade Secretary Julia Lopez said: "Labour have been a disaster for youth jobs. Their tax hikes and red tape have made it harder for businesses to hire, invest and grow, destroying opportunities for young people looking to take their first step on the career ladder."

What does Neet stand for and why does the UK have so many?

Burnham confirmed the long-awaited full review of young people and work will be published next month, and vowed to take its recommendations "seriously".

The review's author, former health secretary Alan Milburn, has argued for the need to "redistribute money from the welfare system to more employment support" in an interview with the Guardian published on Sunday.

"This is not a workshy, snowflake generation," Milburn said. "If we provide more opportunities and we provide more support, the overwhelming majority of young people will take that, because that's what they want. The system isn't delivering what young people want, which is a job."

Milburn calculated that the government spends 25 times more on benefits for young people than getting them into work, describing the current rate of Neets as "shameful" .

Chancellor John Healey, who is due to hand down his first budget on 28 October, told the Labour party conference in September the government had a "moral duty" to address welfare spending.

articles.title: Tiger Shroff: Bollywood actor survives shooting in Mumbai
articles.summary: Video published by several news outlets shows gunmen firing multiple shots at a car while it is moving past a crowd.
articles.body:
Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff has survived a shooting in Mumbai and has not sustained any gunshot wounds, according to Indian police who are investigating the incident.

The 36-year-old was shot at on Sunday evening, while he was in a car that was leaving a football club in the suburb of Juhu.

Several news outlets have published a video showing at least two gunmen firing multiple shots at close range at the front passenger seat of a car while it is slowly moving past a crowd.

The incident has heightened concern about the safety of public figures in India, with some killed or injured in targeted attacks in recent years.

"These attempts to intimidate people will not be tolerated, and we will put an end to this hooliganism," said Eknath Shinde, deputy chief minister of Maharashtra state, where Mumbai is located.

He paid a visit to Shroff after the shooting on Sunday evening, and said the actor and his mother had been left "shaken" by the attack.

Police said two people were injured in the shooting, including Shroff's driver, local media reported.

This is the latest in a string of attacks on some of the country's biggest public figures in recent years.

In 2024, police in India arrested two members of a criminal gang for a gun attack targeting the home of Bollywood actor Salman Khan.

That same year, influential Indian politician Baba Siddique was shot dead in Mumbai.

The son of two actors, Tiger Shroff made his acting debut in 2014 with the romance film Heropanti and went on to star in several films.

He is also a football enthusiast who plays for the professional football club Mumbay FC.

articles.title: China economy: Growth accelerates as AI export boom outweighs domestic weakness
articles.summary: Exports have helped offset weak spending at home, but trade tensions and AI doubts cloud its outlook.
articles.body:
China's economic growth picked up in the three months to the end of September, rebounding from a three-year low as the artificial intelligence (AI) boom helped boost exports.

The world's second largest economy grew by 4.5% in the third quarter, up from the previous period but below the 5% expansion recorded from January to March, according to official Chinese data.

The latest figure is at the bottom end of Beijing's annual growth target of 4.5%-5%, which analysts have said gives policymakers room to address the country's economic challenges.

While exports have helped offset weak spending at home, global trade tensions and uncertainty over AI investments are clouding its outlook.

China's National Bureau of Statistics said on Monday that the economy "sustained steady development against pressure" and showed "momentum with new growth drivers and improving structure".

With exports climbing, China's trade surplus - the amount of goods and services it sells abroad compared to what it buys from other countries - is on track to overtake the record $1.2tn (£900bn) seen last year.

But property investment fell by more than 20% in the first nine months from the same period last year, official data also showed.

Oxford Economics researcher Sheana Yue said manufacturing and high-tech exports have boosted China's growth, despite weak investment and domestic spending.

China's economy has struggling to shake off a long-running property slump, after years of overbuilding and excessive borrowing by private developers.

There are still no signs that this trend will end soon, Yue said.

Trade uncertainties and geopolitical issues have also made Chinese consumers more "pessimistic" and unwilling to spend, she added.

'Investing in people': Can China's new push to boost spending revive the economy?

Faisal Islam: Why China and AI are worrying global finance bosses

The technology industry has been a key driver of China's growth in recent quarters.

Global demand for computer chips and other components used to build AI data centres has helped to ease pressure on Beijing and cushion the impact of sluggish domestic consumption.

Chinese businesses have leaned heavily on exports as a prolonged property slump, weak wage growth and high youth unemployment have weighed on consumer spending at home.

In September, Beijing unveiled a raft of support measures, including lower interest rates for some businesses and subsidies for property buyers, in an effort to boost the economy.

But Beijing is facing a backlash from Western economies - including the US and European Union - as manufacturers struggle to compete with large amounts of cheap Chinese goods.

There are also concerns over the billions of dollars being spent on AI infrastructure and whether the companies making those investments can deliver on their promises of generating huge profits.
